title: Quantification of Coral Chlorophyll Using Shimadzu UV-VIS 2450 Spectrophotometer
author: Rowan McLachlan
materials: Connect the UV-VIS instrument to the UV Probe software. Open the UV Probe software by double-clicking the icon on the desktop (Fig. 9A). Click on the Connect button (Fig. 9B). This will initiate a series of performance checks and will take approximately 10 minutes to complete. When this is complete, click “OK”. Fig. 9. UV Probe software icons to A) open UV Probe software and B) connect the software to the UV-VIS spectrophotometer.

Assemble the filtration equipment. Assemble the vacuum-filtration system assembly: funnel (250 ml), glass fritted base (47 mm diameter), GF/F filter, metal clamp, rubber stopper, disposable test tube, side-arm Erlenmeyer flask (Fig. 18). Note: by placing a foam ring inside the side-arm Erlenmeyer flask, this supports the test tube, and prevents it from falling over or breaking. Fig. 18. Components of the vacuum assembly. The side-arm Erlenmeyer flask is connected to an electronic vacuum pump (not shown in the image above). The GF/F filter is placed between the funnel and the glass frit base, held together with the metal clamp. The glass base is connected to the side-arm Erlenmeyer flask using the blue rubber stopper. Make sure to place a test tube inside the flask before pouring the acetone through the filtration assembly.

steps.title: Grind Frozen Coral Fragments
steps.instruction: Quickly grind frozen coral fragments into a homogenous paste in a mortar to prevent defrosting and degradation (process should take ≤ 5 minutes).

substeps.instruction: Remove coral fragment from -80 °C freezer and place in mortar.
Break fragment into ~1cm3 pieces using a pestle, covering the mortar with a hand to prevent ejection.
Continue crushing until the coral is a homogenous paste resembling hummus.
Gather all paste at the base of the mortar using the pestle.

steps.title: Weigh and Partition Coral Paste
steps.instruction: Measure the total wet weight of the ground coral and isolate a 2 g subsample for chlorophyll analysis.

substeps.instruction: Tare a pre-baked aluminum weighing pan on a balance.
Transfer all ground coral from the mortar to the pan and record the total wet weight (g).
Measure 2 g of wet paste into a pre-labeled 15 ml polypropylene centrifuge tube ('tube A').
Label the tube cap using sticky labels (e.g., ToughSpots TM) to resist acetone vapor.
Record the exact weight of the subsample.
Cap tube A and return to -80 °C freezer to refreeze fully.
Archive remaining material in a separate container (e.g., 5–50 ml Eppendorf tube or cryovial) at -80 °C.

steps.title: Extract Chlorophyll with Acetone
steps.instruction: Perform acetone extraction in a fume hood and total darkness to prevent pigment degradation.

substeps.instruction: Remove sample tubes from freezer and place in a fume hood.
Add 10 ml of 100% acetone (reagent grade/ACS) to each tube using a glass serological pipet and electronic pipet controller (do not use polystyrene pipets).
Cap tubes tightly.
Wrap each tube in at least two layers of aluminum foil (approx. 13 cm2 squares), trimming excess at the base.
Vortex each tube for 30 seconds; if material is stuck to walls, scrape free with a metal spatula and re-vortex.
Return foil-wrapped tubes to -80 °C freezer for storage.

steps.title: Incubate and Centrifuge Samples
steps.instruction: Allow pigments to extract at 4 °C and separate the supernatant from the coral particulate.

substeps.instruction: Refrigerate samples for 24 hours at 4 °C.
Remove tube A from refrigerator and centrifuge for 10 minutes at 3100 x g (4000 rpm in Eppendorf 5810R with rotor A-4 81).
Carefully remove tubes from rotor to avoid mixing particulate matter with supernatant, keeping tubes in foil sleeves.

steps.title: Prepare Spectrophotometer
steps.instruction: Warm up and configure the Shimadzu UV-VIS 2450 spectrophotometer.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the spectrophotometer 30 minutes before use to warm the bulbs.
Clean the four bulbs in the cuvette chamber using lens paper (do not use Kimwipes).
Set acquisition parameters in UV Probe software (Edit → Method):
Attachments tab: Select 6-cell holder (or 'None' for standard 2-cell).
Measurement tab: Set wavelength range to 750–600 nm and sampling interval to 1.0 nm.
Instrument Parameters tab: Set slit width to 0.5 nm.

steps.title: Prepare and Baseline Cuvettes
steps.instruction: Clean quartz cuvettes and set the instrument baseline using 100% acetone.

substeps.instruction: Clean two quartz cuvettes (10 mm optical length) with three rinses of ultrapure deionized water and one rinse of 100% acetone.
Dry the outside of cuvettes with a Kimwipe.
Fill each cuvette with 2 ml of 100% acetone using a 1000 µL pipet.
Place one cuvette in the front (sample) holder and one in the back (reference) holder, ensuring polished windows are parallel to the light beam.
Close the sliding door and click 'Autozero' then 'Baseline' to zero the wavelength range.
Remove the front cuvette, dispose of acetone, and clean the cuvette.

steps.title: Measure Chlorophyll Absorbance
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance of the chlorophyll supernatant across the 750–600 nm range.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the extracted supernatant is at room temperature to prevent condensation.
Using a 1000 µL pipet, fill a cuvette with 2 ml of supernatant, avoiding resuspension of particulate matter.
Load the cuvette into the frontmost holder with frosted sides perpendicular to the light beam.
Click 'Spectrum mode' and 'Start'; the measurement takes approximately 3 minutes.
Save raw absorbance data by clicking 'Data Print', copying to Excel, or using File → Save.
Remove the cuvette and pour the 2 ml subsample back into tube A.
Repeat for all remaining samples, returning to the Spectrum Mode screen and cleaning the cuvette between runs.

steps.title: Perform Second Extraction (Optional)
steps.instruction: If a double extraction is required to capture 100% of pigments, repeat the extraction process.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge tube A again (as per step 15).
Remove the first supernatant with a 10 ml glass serological pipet and transfer to a new labeled 'tube B'.
Add 10 ml of fresh 100% acetone to tube A.
Vortex and refrigerate at 4 °C for 24 hours.
Repeat the measurement steps (centrifugation, cuvette loading, and absorbance reading) for tube A.

steps.title: Filter and Dry Samples for AFDW
steps.instruction: Filter the coral residue and dry it to determine the Ash-Free Dry Weight (AFDW).

substeps.instruction: Pour contents of tubes A and B through a vacuum filtration system with a pre-burned GF/F filter into a glass test tube.
Use a metal spatula to ensure all particulate matter is transferred to the filter.
Transfer the GF/F filter and any residue from the funnel into a pre-labeled aluminum weighing pan.
Place pans in a 60 °C drying oven for 24 hours, including an empty pan with a new GF/F filter as a control.
Remove pans, cool for 10 minutes, and weigh in triplicate (Average Pan + Filter + Dry Residue Weight).

steps.title: Combust Samples and Calculate AFDW
steps.instruction: Burn the dried samples in a muffle furnace to determine organic content.

substeps.instruction: Place dried pans in a muffle furnace and burn at 450 ºC for 5 hours.
Remove pans, cool for 5 minutes, and weigh in triplicate (Average Pan + Filter + Burnt Residue Weight).
Calculate AFDW using: [Δ Coral weight = avg dry pan - avg burnt pan]; [Δ Control weight = avg dry control pan - avg burnt control pan]; [AFDW = Δ Coral weight - Δ Control weight].

steps.title: Calculate Final Chlorophyll Concentration
steps.instruction: Use the absorbance data and AFDW to calculate the normalized chlorophyll concentration.

substeps.instruction: Calculate Chlorophyll a and c2 using Jeffrey & Humphrey (1975) equations: [Chl a = 11.43(E663 - E750) - 0.64(E630 - E750)] and [Chl c2 = 27.09(E630 - E750) - 3.63(E663 - E750)].
Sum the total chlorophyll from the 1st and 2nd extractions.
Normalize to biomass: [Total Chlorophyll per unit biomass (μg gdw-1) = Total Chlorophyll in subsample (ug) ÷ AFDW (g)].

steps.title: Shut Down Instrument
steps.instruction: Properly power down the spectrophotometer after all data is saved.

substeps.instruction: Remove all cuvettes.
Click the 'Disconnect' button in the UV Probe software.
Exit the software and turn off the UV-VIS using the power button.
